# 1 Overview

Second-order spatial point pattern analysis examines the spatial relationships between points in a pattern, specifically focusing on how the presence of one point influences the location of others (eg. 7-11 and Family Marts always open near to each other for the traffics). It goes beyond simply describing the overall density of points (first-order effects) by investigating clustering, dispersion, or randomness at various spatial scales.

Using appropriate functions of [spatstat](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/spatstat/), this hands-on exercise aims to discover the spatial point processes of childecare centres in Singapore.

The specific questions we would like to answer are as follows:

-   are the childcare centres in Singapore randomly distributed throughout the country?

-   if the answer is not, then the next logical question is where are the locations with higher concentration of childcare centres?

# 2 The Data

The data we used is the same as Hands-on Ex2-1:

-   [*Child Care Services*](https://data.gov.sg/datasets?query=Child+Care+Services&resultId=d_2bbcc5e944a9f2d7d40c78097ab652fc&page=1) data from data.gov.sg, a point feature data providing both location and attribute information of childcare centres.
-   [*Master Plan 2019 Subzone Boundary (No Sea)*](https://data.gov.sg/datasets?query=Master+Plan+2019+Subzone+Boundary+(No+Sea)&page=1&resultId=d_0900fdcfdb4666fe2a630f37a532fc06), a polygon feature data providing information of URA 2019 Master Plan Planning Subzone boundary data.

# 5 Second-order Spatial Point Patterns Analysis

In this exercise, we will use four functions to analyze the spatial point patterns:

+---------------------------+------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Function                  | Focus Type | What It Measures                                                | Analogy / Example                                                                 | Remark                                                                                     |
+===========================+============+=================================================================+===================================================================================+============================================================================================+
| `Gest()`                  | **Local**  | Distance from a point to its **nearest neighbor**               | For each childcare centre, how far is the nearest other centre?                   | -   If most centres are **very close** to another → **clustering**                         |
|                           |            |                                                                 |                                                                                   | -   If most centres are **far apart** → **dispersion**                                     |
| Nearest Neighbor Distance |            |                                                                 |                                                                                   |                                                                                            |
+---------------------------+------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `Fest()`                  | **Local**  | Distance from **random spot** to nearest point                  | From random locations in the city, how far is it to the nearest childcare centre? | -   If the city is well-covered, **most locations are close** to a centre → **clustering** |
|                           |            |                                                                 |                                                                                   |                                                                                            |
| Empty Space Function      |            |                                                                 |                                                                                   | -   If large areas are far from a centre → **dispersion**                                  |
+---------------------------+------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `Kest()`                  | **Global** | Counts how many other points are within distance `r` of a point | For every centre, how many others fall within a circle of radius `r`?             | Compares that number to what you'd expect under **random** placement                       |
|                           |            |                                                                 |                                                                                   |                                                                                            |
| Ripley's K Function       |            |                                                                 |                                                                                   |                                                                                            |
+---------------------------+------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| `Lest()`                  | **Global** | Same as K, but easier to interpret                              | Like K, but transformed so a straight line (accumulation) means "no pattern"      | -   If line **stays above** diagonal → clustering                                          |
|                           |            |                                                                 |                                                                                   |                                                                                            |
| L Function                |            |                                                                 |                                                                                   | -   If line **stays below** → regular spacing                                              |
+---------------------------+------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

## 5.1 Analysing Spatial Point Process Using G-Function

The G function measures the distribution of the distances from an arbitrary event to its nearest event. In this section, you will learn how to compute G-function estimation by using [*Gest()*](https://rdrr.io/cran/spatstat/man/Gest.html) of **spatstat** package. You will also learn how to perform monta carlo simulation test using [*envelope()*](https://rdrr.io/cran/spatstat/man/envelope.html) of **spatstat** package

### 5.1.1 Choa Chu Kang planning area

#### 5.1.1.1 Computing G-function estimation



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(1234)
```
:::



The code chunk below is used to compute G-function using *Gest()* of **spatat** package.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
G_CK = Gest(childcare_ck_ppp, correction = "border")
par(bg = "#f6f6f6")
plot(G_CK, xlim=c(0,500))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Hands-on-Ex02_b_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



Since the observed G-function rises **faster** than expected under CSR, it means that points are **closer together than expected**, suggesting a **clustered** spatial pattern. However, we still need further test to conclude if it's clustered.

#### 5.1.1.2 Performing Complete Spatial Randomness Test

To confirm the observed spatial patterns above, a hypothesis test will be conducted. The hypothesis and test are as follows:

-   Ho = The distribution of childcare services at Choa Chu Kang are randomly distributed.
-   H1= The distribution of childcare services at Choa Chu Kang are not randomly distributed.
-   The null hypothesis will be rejected if p-value is smaller than alpha value of 0.001.

Monte Carlo test with G-fucntion:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
G_CK.csr <- envelope(childcare_ck_ppp, Gest, nsim = 999)
```

## 5.2 Analysing Spatial Point Process Using F-Function

In this section, you will learn how to compute F-function estimation by using [*Fest()*](https://rdrr.io/cran/spatstat/man/Fest.html) of **spatstat** package. You will also learn how to perform monta carlo simulation test using [*envelope()*](https://rdrr.io/cran/spatstat/man/envelope.html) of **spatstat** package.

## 5.3 Analysing Spatial Point Process Using K-Function

The K-function measures the number of events found up to a given distance of any particular event. In this section, you will learn how to compute K-function estimates by using [*Kest()*](https://rdrr.io/cran/spatstat/man/Kest.html) of **spatstat**package. You will also learn how to perform monta carlo simulation test using *envelope()* of spatstat package.

### 5.3.1 Choa Chu Kang planning area

#### 5.3.1.1 Computing K-function estimation

The code chunk below is used to compute K-function using *Kest()* of **spatat** package.



::: {.cell}


## 5.4 Analysing Spatial Point Process Using L-Function

In this section, we will learn how to compute L-function estimation by using [*Lest()*](https://rdrr.io/cran/spatstat/man/Lest.html) of **spatstat** package. You will also learn how to perform monta carlo simulation test using *envelope()* of spatstat package.

### 5.4.1 Choa Chu Kang planning area

#### 5.4.1.1 Computing L-function estimation

The code chunk below is used to compute K-function using *Lest()* of **spatat** package.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
L_ck = Lest(childcare_ck_ppp, correction = "Ripley")

par(bg = "#f6f6f6")
plot(L_ck, . -r ~ r, 
     ylab= "L(d)-r", xlab = "d(m)")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Hands-on-Ex02_b_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-28-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



#### 5.4.1.2 Performing Complete Spatial Randomness Test

To confirm the observed spatial patterns above, a hypothesis test will be conducted. The hypothesis and test are as follows:

-   Ho = The distribution of childcare services at Choa Chu Kang are randomly distributed.
-   H1= The distribution of childcare services at Choa Chu Kang are not randomly distributed.
-   The null hypothesis will be rejected if p-value is smaller than alpha value of 0.001.

Monte Carlo test with F-fucntion:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
L_ck.csr <- envelope(childcare_ck_ppp, Lest, nsim = 99, rank = 1, glocal=TRUE)
```
